lead.headline: Binance Hackers Launder $149M via Coinjoins as Abu Dhabi Court Freezes $6.5B in Parallel Recovery Play
lead.tldr: The week's throughline: infrastructure for illicit fund movement is maturing faster than the legal frameworks designed to stop it, while institutional capital keeps flowing to on-chain finance primitives that assume compliance will eventually catch up.

intro: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, this week the gap between how fast stolen crypto moves and how slowly courts can freeze it became a measurable investment variable.

top_signals.title: Binance hack laundering ramps up as $149 million in bitcoin mixed through coinjoins: Elliptic
top_signals.summary: Attackers have begun laundering funds from a major Binance hack, mixing $149 million in Bitcoin via coinjoins. The broader exploit involved the movement of $860 million in Ether, which was partially swapped for Bitcoin to obscure the trail.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Coinjoin volume at this scale signals that privacy infrastructure is now robust enough to absorb nine-figure laundering operations, which reprices the risk premium on exchange custody and on-chain AML tooling.

top_signals.title: Binance hacker moves nearly $600M in ETH, routes funds through THORChain, Chainflip
top_signals.summary: Hackers associated with a Binance exploit have moved nearly $600 million in ETH. The attackers are utilizing THORChain and Chainflip to obfuscate the movement of the stolen funds.
top_signals.why_it_matters: THORChain and Chainflip being the chosen rails for $600M in obfuscated ETH movement validates cross-chain DEX infrastructure as critical plumbing, but also flags regulatory targeting risk for any protocol enabling non-KYC swaps at scale.

top_signals.title: Binance hackers stole 192 tokens across 11 networks, court docs show
top_signals.summary: Court documents have revealed detailed specifics regarding a massive $6.3 billion hack of Binance. The theft involved 192 different tokens across 11 networks, including over $3.46 billion in stablecoins.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The 192-token, 11-network scope of the Binance breach reveals how multi-chain complexity amplifies attack surface in ways that single-chain security audits cannot capture, raising the bar for portfolio risk assessment.

top_signals.title: Bain Capital Crypto leads $110M Variational round at $1.5B valuation
top_signals.summary: Variational has raised $110 million in a funding round led by Bain Capital Crypto, achieving a valuation of $1.5 billion. The company aims to bridge traditional financial liquidity with on-chain traders and target brokerage customers.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Bain Capital Crypto's $110M bet on Variational at $1.5B implies institutional allocators are underwriting on-chain brokerage infrastructure as if regulatory clarity on tokenized securities is a when-not-if, despite current SEC ambiguity.

top_signals.title: Binance says it won $6.5B worldwide freezing order after hack
top_signals.summary: Binance has successfully obtained a $6.5 billion worldwide freezing order from an Abu Dhabi court. The order is intended to assist in the recovery of digital assets stolen during a hack in October.
top_signals.why_it_matters: A $6.5B worldwide freezing order from an Abu Dhabi court is a novel jurisdictional play that tests whether on-chain asset recovery can be enforced through off-chain legal pressure on service providers.

top_signals.title: Binance obtains $6.5 billion freezing order from Abu Dhabi court in bid to recover stolen crypto
top_signals.summary: Binance has secured a $6.5 billion freezing order from a court in Abu Dhabi to recover stolen cryptocurrency. The order allows for on-chain service and provides a legal framework for partners to return the frozen assets.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The explicit provision for 'on-chain service' in this freezing order suggests courts are learning to write crypto-native enforcement language, which could standardize faster than expected if upheld.

deals.summary: Variational has raised $110 million in a funding round led by Bain Capital Crypto, achieving a valuation of $1.5 billion. The company aims to bridge traditional financial liquidity with on-chain traders and target brokerage customers.

Payward, the parent company of Kraken, is acquiring Tribe Capital to integrate private-market capabilities into its platform. The move allows Payward to expand into private-market sourcing, underwriting, and fund management.

Codex has raised $30 million in funding to streamline international payments between Asia and global markets using stablecoins. The startup aims to replace expensive traditional payment infrastructure with blockchain-based solutions.

The Solana Foundation has acquired a majority interest in the crypto data aggregator CoinGecko. This strategic move aims to support CoinGecko's expansion and integrate DeFi and trading experiences specifically tied to the Solana ecosystem.

Stablecoin infrastructure provider Avenia has raised $25 million in a Series A extension round led by Lightspeed Faction. The company intends to use the capital for product development and potential acquisitions.

on_the_radar.title: World Bank partners with Circle, Citi to explore stablecoins for payments
on_the_radar.summary: The World Bank has entered a partnership with Circle and Citi to investigate the use of stablecoin infrastructure. The initiative aims to facilitate faster and more cost-effective payments, specifically targeting development finance.

on_the_radar.title: Hackers inject credit card, crypto-stealing malware into 178 major websites
on_the_radar.summary: Cybercriminals have injected credit card and cryptocurrency-stealing malware into scripts across 178 major websites. High-profile organizations including Ledger, BBC, and IKEA were among those affected by the attack.

on_the_radar.title: Zelle taps Solana for stablecoin-based international expansion
on_the_radar.summary: Zelle has announced plans to utilize its ZLUSD stablecoin on the Solana blockchain to facilitate international expansion. The company is currently conducting private transfer testing as part of this strategic move.

on_the_radar.title: DBS, JPMorgan’s Kinexys launch 24/7 transfers of tokenized deposits
on_the_radar.summary: DBS and JPMorgan's Kinexys have launched a new service enabling 24/7 transfers of tokenized US dollar deposits between Singapore and the United States. This integration leverages blockchain technology to remove traditional banking time constraints for institutional clients.

on_the_radar.title: ECB seeks industry partners for tokenized deposits, securities experiments
on_the_radar.summary: The European Central Bank (ECB) is seeking industry partners for its Appia initiative to experiment with tokenized deposits and securities. Financial firms are invited to apply by December 11 to participate in these trials.

on_the_radar.title: Hong Kong pushes to bring crypto custodians, advisers under licensing rules
on_the_radar.summary: Hong Kong has introduced a new bill to expand its cryptocurrency licensing framework. The proposal aims to bring custody, advisory, dealing, and management services under the formal oversight of the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC).

on_the_radar.title: Sky Protocol sees $2 billion in stablecoin withdrawals, disputes illicit fund claims
on_the_radar.summary: Sky Protocol is facing significant outflows with $2 billion in stablecoin withdrawals from its USDS asset. The protocol maintains that the stablecoin has held its peg and is actively disputing claims that the transactions are linked to illicit activity.

on_the_radar.title: Senate passes first-ever prediction market bill as Democrats turn up heat on upstart industry
on_the_radar.summary: The Senate has passed the DEATH BETS Act, the first-ever bill specifically targeting prediction markets. The legislation aims to outlaw wagers tied to war and death, signaling increased regulatory pressure on the industry.

on_the_radar.title: US Senate advances prediction market restrictions with DEATH BETS Act
on_the_radar.summary: The US Senate has advanced the DEATH BETS Act, which aims to ban prediction market contracts involving war, assassination, and death. The legislation is driven by concerns over insider trading and the ethics of betting on catastrophic events.

on_the_radar.title: Lagarde warns Europe could miss chance to unify tokenized markets
on_the_radar.summary: ECB President Christine Lagarde has cautioned that Europe must act quickly to establish a unified regulatory framework for tokenized markets. She warned that failure to do so could lead to market fragmentation and a missed opportunity to leverage tokenization benefits.

on_the_radar.title: MoonPay seeks US bank charter for stablecoin, custody services
on_the_radar.summary: MoonPay is seeking federal approval to establish a national trust bank based in Miami. This move aims to integrate stablecoin and custody services directly into a regulated US banking framework.

on_the_radar.title: Trump’s SEC nominee Johnson backs formal rulemaking for tokenized stock trading
on_the_radar.summary: SEC nominee Kristin Johnson has expressed support for establishing formal rulemaking to govern the trading of tokenized stocks. Additionally, Steven Levine highlighted the agency's ability to provide exemptions for such activities.

worth_a_read.note: Aikido's €4bn target from Storonsky's backing is a datapoint on whether European security software valuations have decoupled from fundamentals or if AI-native security justifies the premium.

worth_a_read.note: Polygon's token holder concentration and staking flows in Q3 will inform whether the chain's institutional partnerships are translating into sticky token demand.

linkedin_post:
The Binance hackers have now moved $149 million through coinjoins and nearly $600 million via THORChain and Chainflip. Same week, an Abu Dhabi court froze $6.5 billion worldwide. The same week.

We are watching two infrastructures race. One is built to obscure: coinjoins, cross-chain DEXs, multi-network swaps across 192 tokens. The other is built to recover: freezing orders with on-chain service provisions, legal frameworks that let partners return assets without becoming defendants themselves.

The Abu Dhabi order is the more interesting signal. Courts are learning to write crypto-native enforcement. If this holds, the cost of laundering stolen funds rises not because the tech fails, but because the service providers holding the exits get served. That reprices the risk model for any protocol enabling non-KYC swaps.

Meanwhile Bain Capital Crypto put $110 million into Variational at $1.5 billion. The bet assumes institutional liquidity will flow on-chain through regulated brokerage pipes. That only works if the compliance infrastructure wins this race.

What would kill this thesis: a major freezing order gets ignored by a jurisdiction that actually hosts the assets. What would confirm it: a service provider complying voluntarily because the legal language is clear enough to make fighting expensive.

We are underwriting the gap between those two outcomes.
